additions.title: Moses invites Pharaoh to set the time for removing the frogs
additions.reason: Moses' imperative 'Appoint a time for me' answers Pharaoh's request (AUD-02-8-4); the catalogue records this exchange's directions and offers nearby.

additions.title: God tells Moses to set the ordinances before Israel
additions.reason: Heading charge ('ordinances which you shall set before them'), recorded like ot-exodus-v19-6 and ot-numbers-v5-12; only broad torah-exodus-21-1 includes it.

additions.title: Bring in and arrange the table and the lampstand
additions.reason: Editor rejected C0275 (no designated sides); as an installation step it gets its own record, like C0368–C0370 for Exodus 40:5–8.

additions.title: Sisera summons his chariots and army to the Kishon
additions.reason: Reported muster order with stated forces and destination, recorded like Jabin’s reported summons (AUD-06-11-1); Sisera’s own order, not a fulfilment.

additions.title: Gideon rallies Abiezer and sends messengers to call the other tribes
additions.reason: Gideon’s trumpet and dispatch of messengers rally the named groups. The surrounding statement about God’s Spirit does not quote a separate divine muster order.
additions.audience: Abiezer; the men of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun and Naphtali

additions.title: Shechem's men and Maallon's house make Abimelech king at Shechem
additions.reason: Narrated king-making with a named appointee, like published AUD-10-2-8 (Abner makes Ish-bosheth king); Jotham's rebuke (AUD-07-9-16) recalls it.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.speaker_or_source: all the men of Shechem and the house of Maallon (Millo)

additions.title: Jephthah’s daughter tells her father to fulfil his vow concerning her
additions.reason: She expressly tells Jephthah to carry out what he had vowed concerning her. The vow is his, and her distinct request for a period to mourn is already recorded in verse 37.

additions.title: Micah installs one of his sons as priest of his shrine
additions.reason: Reported priestly installation (“filled the hand”), an appointment like Jeroboam’s priests (AUD-11-13-33). Topic changed to Sanctuary, priesthood and ministry.

additions.title: Israel arranges a smoke signal with the ambush at Gibeah
additions.reason: The prearranged signal is stated in 20:38. Reference narrowed from 20:38–40, since 20:39–40 narrate the battle and the signal’s fulfilment.

additions.title: Saul tells Ahijah the priest to withdraw his hands
additions.reason: Editor: 'Withdraw your hands' is a separate command from bringing the ephod (ot-1-samuel-v14-18); recorded separately as Saul breaks off the inquiry.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Saul sentences Abimelech and his father’s house to death
additions.reason: Saul addresses the death sentence to Abimelech. The next verse gives the separate execution order addressed to Saul’s runners, which they refuse.
additions.audience: Abimelech the priest, concerning himself and his father’s house

additions.title: David asks Saul to recognize that he spared him and leave judgment to the Lord
additions.reason: David’s cloak evidence and imperative to recognize his innocence are specific to this scene. His prayer for the Lord’s judgment belongs to the same appeal. The separate proverb in verse 14 is already indexed.

additions.title: The Lord repays with good the one who sends away an enemy safely
additions.reason: Saul states this as a general maxim and applies it to David sparing him. The wisdom is spoken by Saul in this exchange.

additions.title: Nabal’s servant urges Abigail to act before disaster strikes
additions.reason: The servant urges Abigail to decide what to do in response to impending danger. He gives urgent counsel and leaves the action to her.

additions.title: David sends spies to ascertain Saul’s arrival
additions.reason: Reported reconnaissance commission with a clear task, like David’s reported sending to inquire (AUD-10-11-3) and the catalogue’s spy commissions.

additions.title: The Lord repays each person’s righteousness and faithfulness
additions.reason: General maxim on divine recompense spoken in narrative, recorded as Wisdom like AUD-09-17-45 and AUD-09-24-14.

additions.title: Saul asks the summoned Samuel to tell him what to do
additions.reason: Saul explicitly asks Samuel to tell him what he should do after his other inquiries had received no answer. Retain this as a historical request by Saul in the prohibited consultation setting.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.audience: Samuel, brought up by the medium

additions.title: Hadadezer summons Syrian forces from beyond the river
additions.reason: Reported summons of allied forces, recorded like Jabin’s reported coalition summons (AUD-06-11-1). Link 1 Chronicles 19:16 as its parallel.
additions.audience: the Syrians beyond the River, under Shobach

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel describes Syrian messengers bringing the forces from beyond the river under Shobach.

additions.title: Joab finally lets Ahimaaz run after Cushi
additions.reason: Editor: Joab's 'Run' is a separate directive from Ahimaaz's request (ot-2-samuel-v18-22); recorded as the permission answering the earlier refusal (ot-2-samuel-v18-19).
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: David appoints Benaiah to receive his instructions
additions.reason: Reported appointment, recorded like AUD-11-2-35 and AUD-09-18-13. Link 1 Chronicles 11:25 (also open as R8a V051) as the parallel.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel describes David appointing Benaiah over his ancestral house. Samuel instead describes him receiving David’s instructions.

additions.title: Solomon levies Israelite workers for Lebanon in rotating shifts
additions.reason: Verses 27–28 identify the levy and specify how Solomon dispatches it, with Adoniram overseeing the workers. The following census of other workers does not add a quoted command.
additions.audience: the levy from all Israel under Adoniram, and the appointed overseers

additions.title: Solomon puts Jeroboam over the burdens of Joseph’s house
additions.reason: Reported appointment, recorded like AUD-09-18-13 and AUD-11-2-35. Link 1 Kings 12:24b, which retells it.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additional_scripture.context_note: This continuation recounts Solomon assigning Jeroboam the burdens of Joseph’s house.

additions.title: Israel rejects David’s house and calls its men to their tents
additions.reason: The people’s call to desert David’s house for their tents; same kind as published AUD-10-20-1 (Sheba), but a separate speaker and occasion.

additions.title: Israel summons Jeroboam to the assembly and makes him king
additions.reason: Stated appointment of a king by the assembly, as the catalogue records at AUD-10-2-4 and AUD-10-5-1; no current record.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Rehoboam musters Judah and Benjamin to fight the house of Israel
additions.reason: Reported muster for war, like published AUD-09-13-2 and AUD-09-23-8; countermanded by ot-1-kings-v12-23. Parallels listed as Additional Scripture.
additions.audience: the assembly of Judah and Benjamin (120,000 warriors)

additions.title: The old prophet tells his sons to saddle his donkey
additions.reason: Direct household order; the catalogue records this kind nearby (AUD-12-4-22, ot-2-kings-v4-24, AUD-11-13-31). Weak, hence low.

additions.title: Israel’s army makes its commander Omri king in the camp
additions.reason: Stated king-making by the army, the kind recorded at AUD-10-2-4 and AUD-10-2-8; 1 Kings 16 has no records.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.speaker_or_source: the people in Israel’s camp at Gibbethon

additions.title: Elijah asks the widow for water and a morsel of bread
additions.reason: Editor: separate requests for water and bread, distinct from the cake request (ot-1-kings-v17-13); recorded separately. 17:12 is the widow's reply, no direction.

additions.title: Elijah tells Baal’s prophets to move away so he can offer
additions.reason: Direct order to Baal’s prophets (‘Move away now’); Elijah’s neighbouring orders at 18:25, 18:27, 18:30 and 18:34 are all recorded.

additions.title: The son of Ader asks Ahab through his attendants to spare him
additions.reason: The attendants relay the Syrian king’s own plea. Verse 31 gives the separate planning conversation before the delegation reaches Ahab.
additions.speaker_or_source: The son of Ader, speaking through his attendants

additions.title: Ahab adjures Micaiah to speak only truth in the Lord’s name
additions.reason: An adjuration demanding truth under oath, not a mere rhetorical question; compare ot-1-samuel-v3-17. Chronicles parallel listed.

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel gives the king’s adjuration that Micaiah speak truth in the Lord’s name.

additions.title: The army herald tells each man to return to his city and land
additions.reason: The herald’s proclaimed dismissal of the army is a new order; it echoes, but does not cite, Micaiah’s word (ot-1-kings-v22-17).

additions.title: Elisha tells the sons of the prophets to keep silent
additions.reason: Elisha’s order ‘Be silent’ is unrecorded. Reference narrowed to 2:3, 5, since 2:4 belongs to AUD-12-2-2.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.audience: the sons of the prophets at Bethel and Jericho

additions.title: Jehoram asks Jehoshaphat to join his war against Moab
additions.reason: Jehoram’s question is an actual request for military assistance and receives agreement. The next verse switches to deciding the route.

additions.title: Moab’s troops urge one another to plunder the allied camp
additions.reason: Troops urging one another to act, the kind recorded at ot-1-samuel-v4-9; a brief battle cry, hence low.

additions.title: Elisha commissions Gehazi to ask the Shunammite what help she wants
additions.reason: Elisha directs Gehazi to deliver an offer of help; distinct from the summons at ot-2-kings-v4-12, and Elisha’s orders nearby are recorded.
additions.audience: Gehazi, with a message for the Shunammite woman

additions.title: Elisha sends Gehazi to ask after the Shunammite’s family
additions.reason: Direct errand order to Gehazi; Elisha’s neighbouring orders to him (4:12, 4:27, 4:29) are recorded.

additions.title: Syria’s king writes Israel’s king to cure Naaman of his leprosy
additions.reason: Editor: the letter conveys a different direction to Israel's king than ot-2-kings-v5-5's sending; recorded as its own royal letter.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.speaker_or_source: the king of Syria, by letter

additions.title: An attendant advises sending horsemen to scout the abandoned camp
additions.reason: Counsel to the king, recorded as Instruction as at ot-1-kings-v21-31 and ot-1-kings-v1-2; the king’s resulting commission is ot-2-kings-v7-14.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.speaker_or_source: one of the king of Israel’s attendants

additions.title: Joram orders his chariot yoked to go and meet Jehu
additions.reason: Direct order (‘Yoke up!’), carried out; Joram’s and Jehu’s orders in this scene (9:17–19) are recorded.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Jehu’s letter dares Samaria’s leaders to crown Ahab’s son and fight
additions.reason: Written imperative challenge, like ot-2-kings-v14-8; distinct from the second letter’s order at AUD-12-10-6.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.audience: the rulers, elders and guardians of Ahab’s sons in Samaria

additions.title: Jehoiada crowns and anoints the boy Joash as king
additions.reason: Stated anointing and coronation, recorded separately from the call to reign (AUD-14-23-3), as with Jehu and Saul. Chronicles parallel listed.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel names Jehoiada and his sons at the boy’s coronation and anointing.

additions.title: Judah’s people make the sixteen-year-old Azariah king
additions.reason: Stated king-making by the people, the kind recorded at AUD-10-2-4. Chronicles parallel 2 Chronicles 26:1 is item U11655 elsewhere.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel calls the sixteen-year-old appointee Uzziah and likewise names Judah’s people as making him king.

additions.title: Ahaz sends Uriah the Damascus altar’s design for construction
additions.reason: A building pattern sent for copying, like AUD-13-28-11; 16:11 expressly cites it. Distinct from the sacrifice order at ot-2-kings-v16-15.

additions.title: Hezekiah asks Assyria’s king to withdraw and accepts the imposed tribute
additions.reason: Explicit request (‘Withdraw from me’) with submission to tribute; royal appeals like ot-2-kings-v16-7 are recorded. Nothing covers this verse.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.audience: Sennacherib king of Assyria at Lachish
additions.speaker_or_source: Hezekiah king of Judah, through messengers

additions.title: The Assyrian envoy calls Judah to join Assyria and offers horses if it can provide riders
additions.reason: The envoy’s imperative taunt is the one unrecorded directive in a speech whose other verses are recorded. Isaiah parallel listed.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel likewise invites an alliance and offers two thousand horses if Judah can provide riders.

additions.title: The Lord designates Jeroboam to rule Israel and calls him to faithful obedience
additions.reason: The Lord through Ahijah designates Jeroboam to reign in verse 37. In verse 38 the Lord’s abiding support and faithful dynasty depend on Jeroboam’s obedience. The text does not impose that condition on the initial kingship.
additions.speaker_or_source: the Lord, through Ahijah the Shilonite

additions.title: Hezekiah asks Isaiah for a sign and chooses the shadow’s return
additions.reason: A request to the prophet, not a prayer, like AUD-11-13-6; Isaiah 38:22 here is a statement, not the request.

additions.title: Manasseh appoints a charmer and spirit-mediums
additions.reason: Stated wicked appointment, comparable to AUD-11-13-33 and AUD-02-1-11, though set in a list of sins. Audience corrected to Personal.

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel reports Manasseh appointing spirit-mediums and enchanters in a list of his other practices.

additions.title: The people of the land make Josiah king after Amon’s murder
additions.reason: Stated king-making by the people of the land, the kind recorded at AUD-10-2-4. Chronicles parallel listed.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additional_scripture.context_note: The same succession follows the killing of Amon’s conspirators. The people of the land make Josiah king.

additions.title: Josiah summons Judah’s elders and reads the covenant book to all
additions.reason: The reported royal summons is specifically to the elders. Verse 2 describes the separate public reading of the covenant book to all the people.
additions.audience: The elders of Judah and Jerusalem, who were summoned

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel likewise distinguishes the king’s summons to the elders from the reading of the book to the assembled people.

additions.title: The people of the land anoint Joachas and make him king
additions.reason: Stated anointing and king-making by the people, the kind recorded at AUD-10-2-4. Chronicles parallel 2 Chronicles 36:1 is item U11919 elsewhere.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel uses the spelling Joahaz and also reports his appointment by the people of the land.

additions.title: Pharaoh Nechao makes Eliakim king and renames him Joakim
additions.reason: A foreign king installs and renames a vassal, a stated appointment like AUD-10-2-8. Chronicles 36:4 parallel listed; its tribute clauses belong elsewhere.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel spells the names Pharaoh Neco and Jehoiakim. It records the same replacement and renaming.

additions.title: Nebuchadnezzar appoints Gedaliah over those left in Judah
additions.reason: Explicit appointment of a governor; Gedaliah’s own counsel is recorded (ot-2-kings-v25-24) but not his appointment. Reports listed as Additional Scripture.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: David divides the Levites into service courses
additions.reason: Verse 6 explicitly identifies David as dividing the Levites into service courses. Verses 3–5 supply the census and offices without quoting David assigning each individual office.
additions.audience: the Levites aged thirty and upward

additions.title: Hiram tells Solomon to bring the rafted timber from Joppa to Jerusalem
additions.reason: Editor: the timber-transport arrangement is a distinct instruction from Hiram's provisions request (ot-2-chronicles-v2-14); recorded separately. Kings parallel: 1 Kings 5:23.
additions.speaker_or_source: Chiram (Hiram) king of Tyre, by letter

additional_scripture.context_note: Hiram’s parallel message describes sending the timber in rafts and Solomon taking it away from the specified place.

additions.title: Solomon rules his Egyptian wife may not live in David’s city
additions.reason: Solomon explicitly states his wife shall not live in David’s city and gives the reason. The narrative reports that he moved her and does not identify the hearers of the quoted ruling.
additions.audience: Concerning Pharaoh’s daughter, Solomon’s wife. The person addressed is unidentified.

additions.title: The Lord shows strength for wholehearted people, Hanani tells Asa
additions.reason: Hanani’s rebuke names Asa’s reliance on Syria and contrasts it with the Lord’s support for wholehearted trust. The source names Hanani as speaker without quoting a direct divine oracle.

additions.title: Jehoshaphat appoints leaders in Judah and the captured cities of Ephraim
additions.reason: Stated appointment of leaders and garrisons, like AUD-09-8-1; unnamed appointees and no stated charge, hence low.
additions.audience: his forces and the leaders set over Judah’s and Ephraim’s cities

additions.title: Jehu orders his men to search for Ahaziah
additions.reason: Chronicles explicitly reports the search order. Capture and death follow. The Kings account reports a differently framed pursuit and should not be filed as wording of this same order.

additions.title: Hezekiah directs Aaron’s priests to offer for all Israel
additions.reason: Verse 21 reports Hezekiah telling the priests to approach the altar, and verse 24 quotes his direction that the offerings cover all Israel.

additions.title: Hezekiah orders the burnt offering, begun with song and trumpets
additions.reason: Reported order to offer the burnt offering, distinct from the instrument arrangement at AUD-14-29-25. Reference corrected: 29:28 is fulfilment narrative.

additions.title: Hezekiah and the assembly issue a call to keep Passover in the second month
additions.reason: Verses 2–5 describe a specific decision and public proclamation when priests and people were not ready. The standing second-month provision in Numbers 9 and the quoted appeal in 2 Chronicles 30:6 are distinct.
additions.audience: all Israel and Judah, from Beersheba to Dan
additions.speaker_or_source: King Hezekiah, his rulers and the assembly in Jerusalem

additions.title: Hezekiah appoints commanders of war over the people
additions.reason: Narrated appointment of war commanders, like AUD-10-18-1; leads into the recorded 32:7 speech. Note: 32:8 completes that speech (extend ot-2-chronicles-v32-7).
additions.audience: the commanders of war over the people

additions.title: Josiah assigns the priests to their watches for temple service
additions.reason: Narrated assignment of the priests to their courses for Josiah's Passover, parallel in kind to AUD-14-31-2 (Hezekiah); distinct from the Levites' charge (35:3–6).

additions.title: Pharaoh Neco orders a tribute of silver and gold from Judah
additions.reason: Verse 4a identifies the assessment as being at Pharaoh’s command. This is the historical royal levy. The parallel Saints readings differ on the amount of gold.

additional_scripture.context_note: Both accounts report Pharaoh imposing a levy. Chronicles gives one talent of gold and Kings gives one hundred. Both give one hundred talents of silver.

additions.title: Nebuchadnezzar appoints Zedekiah king and binds him by oath
additions.reason: Narrated king-making with the oath Nebuchadnezzar imposed (36:13), like AUD-10-2-8; 2 Kings 24:17 is the unrecorded parallel.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel reports the king of Babylon making Mattaniah king and changing his name to Zedekiah. Chronicles adds that the king made Zedekiah swear by God.

additions.title: Dying Alexander divides his kingdom among his officers
additions.reason: Deathbed transfer of rule to his officers, the kind of appointment the catalogue records (AUD-15-6-14, AUD-16-9-23); 1:8 shows its outworking.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Antiochus orders Judah’s cities to sacrifice city by city
additions.reason: This states the particular city-by-city execution order following the earlier general decree. The appointment of overseers is narrated alongside it.

additions.title: Antiochus pays his army a year’s wages and orders it ready
additions.reason: Reported royal muster and order to the paid army to stand ready; uncovered, and distinct from the Lysias commission (AUD-15-3-32).

additions.title: Judas sends men to spy out Timothy’s camp
additions.reason: Narrated sending of spies, with their report, as the catalogue records for AUD-06-7-2 and AUD-04-21-32.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Judas asks the people of Ephron to let his company pass through
additions.reason: Request for passage in the same 'We will pass through your land' form the catalogue records at AUD-04-21-21 (Numbers 21:21–22); refused.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Judas orders his company to encamp where each man stands
additions.reason: Reported order by proclamation with stated content before the assault on Ephron; uncovered, like ot-1-maccabees-v5-42.

additions.title: Lysias makes the young Antiochus king and names him Eupator
additions.reason: Narrated king-making that sets aside Antiochus's appointment of Philip (AUD-15-6-14); king-makings are recorded (AUD-10-2-8).
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Judas assembles all the people to besiege the citadel
additions.reason: Corrected to 6:19: narrated summons to besiege, like published AUD-09-23-8 (Saul at Keilah); 6:20 is fulfilment narrative.

additions.title: Opponents of Judas urge the king to avenge their brothers and act quickly
additions.reason: The petition asks the king to give judgment and avenge their brothers, then presses him to act quickly. The intervening verses recount the petitioners’ stated grievances.
additions.speaker_or_source: ungodly men from Israel with escapees from the citadel

additions.title: Antiochus Eupator breaks his oath and orders Zion’s wall pulled down
additions.reason: Reported order with stated content, breaking the sworn terms of 6:60–61; uncovered.

additions.title: Bacchides places the country under Alcimus with a supporting force
additions.reason: Narrated handover of the country's government to Alcimus with a force, distinct from his priesthood (AUD-15-7-8); appointments are in scope.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Judas sends envoys to Rome to seek alliance and friendship
additions.reason: Judas's embassy to Rome with the envoys' request to the senate (8:20); uncovered. Like AUD-15-12-1; the treaty itself is AUD-15-8-24.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.audience: Eupolemus and Jason, who were sent as envoys to the Roman senate

additions.title: Bacchides appoints the ungodly men as masters of the country
additions.reason: Narrated appointment by a hostile governor (wicked rulers are in scope); 9:26 shows its outworking. Uncovered.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Jonathan sends John to ask the Nabateans to keep their belongings
additions.reason: Jonathan sends his brother on the specific errand of seeking permission to deposit their belongings. Verse 36 supplies John’s name, while describing a separate seizure.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.audience: Jonathan’s brother John, sent to the Nabateans

additions.title: Alcimus orders the wall of the sanctuary’s inner court demolished
additions.reason: Reported order with stated content against the sanctuary; 9:55 records Alcimus struck down. Uncovered.

additions.title: Bacchides secretly writes to his Judean allies to seize Jonathan
additions.reason: Bacchides' own written order to his allies, acting on the lawless men's plot (ot-1-maccabees-v9-58, a different speaker); uncovered.

additions.title: Jonathan sends envoys to Bacchides seeking peace and the captives’ return
additions.reason: Jonathan sends envoys with the stated purposes of arranging peace and recovering captives. Verse 71 reports Bacchides accepting and swearing terms.

additions.title: Alexander writes summoning Jonathan to meet him at Ptolemais
additions.reason: Reported written royal summons; the catalogue records summonses (AUD-01-41-14) and the comparable meeting request at ot-1-maccabees-v10-56.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Alexander orders Jonathan’s garments removed and him clothed in purple
additions.reason: Reported order with stated content, carried out; adding it to ot-1-maccabees-v10-63 (protection order) would change that record's meaning.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Demetrius appoints Apollonius, who was over Coele-Syria
additions.reason: The text explicitly reports the appointment and describes Apollonius as already associated with Coele-Syria. It gives no exact title or quoted terms for the new appointment.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Jonathan commands his army to stand firm under the cavalry ambush
additions.reason: Sole witness to Jonathan's order to stand firm ('as Jonathan had commanded'); compare AUD-06-19-49, built on 'at the Lord's command'. Thin.

additions.title: Alexander orders his cities to welcome Ptolemy as his father-in-law
additions.reason: Explicit reported royal command ('King Alexander had commanded them to meet him'); uncovered.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Demetrius II orders Jonathan to lift the siege and come to Ptolemais
additions.reason: Reported written order with stated content, defied in 11:23; uncovered.

additions.title: Jonathan orders the siege of the citadel to continue
additions.reason: Jonathan's own reported order, defying Demetrius's letter (11:22); a distinct direction, uncovered.
additions.audience: The forces continuing the siege of the citadel

additions.title: Demetrius II confirms Jonathan as high priest and among the First Friends
additions.reason: Narrated royal confirmation in office, like AUD-15-11-57 and AUD-15-10-18; uncovered.

additions.title: Jonathan asks Demetrius to exempt Judea, the three districts, and Samaria from tribute
additions.reason: Verse 28 records Jonathan’s stated request and his offer of three hundred talents. Demetrius’s consent and written grant are distinct responses.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Jonathan asks Demetrius to remove the forces in Jerusalem’s citadel and the strongholds
additions.reason: Reported request with its reason, answered in 11:42–43 (AUD-15-11-42, a different speaker); uncovered.

additions.title: Antiochus VI appoints Simon general from Tyre’s Ladder to Egypt
additions.reason: Separate appointment of Simon; adding it to AUD-15-11-57 (Jonathan's confirmation) would change that record's meaning.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Rome issues letters for Jonathan’s envoys to be escorted safely to Judah
additions.reason: The Roman council issues safe-conduct letters to the authorities in each place. Verse 3 contains the envoys’ separate statement of their mission.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Areus asks Onias to write about his people’s welfare
additions.reason: Verse 22 expressly asks Onias to write. Verse 23 declares shared possessions and separately tells the Spartan messengers to convey the assurance.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.speaker_or_source: Areus king of the Spartans, by letter

additional_scripture.context_note: Jonathan’s letter recalls Areus’s earlier letter to Onias and Onias receiving the envoy.

additions.title: Tryphon sends forces to destroy all Jonathan’s men in Galilee
additions.reason: Reported sending of forces with a stated mission, like published AUD-15-16-17; uncovered.

additions.title: Simon sends Jonathan son of Absalom with a force to Joppa
additions.reason: Reported military commission (sent with a force; Joppa taken); uncovered, like ot-1-maccabees-v5-17.

additions.title: The citadel garrison urges Tryphon to come through the wilderness with food
additions.reason: Reported request carried by envoys; Tryphon acts on it (13:22). Uncovered.

additions.title: Simon sends envoys to Demetrius II to seek remission for the country
additions.reason: Reported embassy with a stated request; Demetrius's reply is AUD-15-13-36, a different speaker. Uncovered.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.audience: The envoys Simon chose and sent to King Demetrius

additions.title: Arsaces sends a commander to capture Demetrius alive
additions.reason: Reported commission with a stated mission (seize Demetrius alive); 14:3 is fulfilment. Typed Commission, like AUD-15-16-17.
additions.speaker_or_source: Arsaces king of Persia and Media

additions.title: Sparta resolves to honor the Jewish envoys and preserve their words in the public records
additions.reason: The Spartan people resolve on specified acts for this diplomatic visit. The decision is recounted to Simon and does not establish a standing rule.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.audience: the Spartans; reported by letter to Simon and the Jews
additions.speaker_or_source: the people of Sparta, by resolution

additions.title: Jeremiah tells the deportees to take some of the altar fire
additions.reason: Distinct reported order (take the fire); adding it to AUD-16-2-2 (remember the law) would change that record. 1:19 narrates its fulfilment.
additions.speaker_or_source: Jeremiah the prophet, as found in the records

additional_scripture.context_note: The earlier account reports priests taking the altar fire and hiding it. It supplies context without quoting Jeremiah’s order.

additions.title: Heliodorus’s companions beg Onias to pray for his life
additions.reason: Reported request to the high priest to intercede, like AUD-29-44-3; Onias acts on it (3:32). Uncovered.

additions.title: Jason’s envoys ask that his money for Heracles not fund sacrifice
additions.reason: Corrected to 4:19: the bearers' reported request with its reason (unfitting); 4:20 is outcome narrative. Uncovered.
additions.audience: those receiving the gift at Tyre
additions.speaker_or_source: the envoys Jason sent to Tyre

additions.title: Antiochus gives Menelaus the high priesthood after he outbids Jason
additions.reason: Royal grant of the high priesthood by 'royal orders' (4:25); 4:23 introduces Menelaus as Jason's envoy. Speaker narrowed to the king.

additions.title: Antiochus summons Menelaus and Sostratus over the unpaid funds
additions.reason: Reported royal summons after Sostratus demanded the unpaid funds; the catalogue records reported summons (AUD-31-5-9, AUD-01-41-14). 4:27 completes the sentence.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.audience: Menelaus the high priest and Sostratus, commander of the citadel

additions.title: The council of elders sends three men to accuse Menelaus
additions.reason: Narrated commission of three delegates to present the case against Menelaus; envoy sendings are recorded (AUD-15-12-1), but this one is incidental.

additions.title: Antiochus leaves Philip and Andronicus as overseers to afflict the people
additions.reason: The account specifically identifies Philip and Andronicus as overseers Antiochus left to afflict the people. It mentions Menelaus separately.
additions.audience: Philip in Jerusalem and Andronicus at Gerizim

additions.title: Apollonius orders his troops to parade under arms on the Sabbath
additions.reason: Apollonius orders his troops to parade under arms on the Sabbath. The next verse reports the killings that followed.

additions.title: Antiochus tries to force seven brothers and their mother to eat forbidden pork
additions.reason: The opening reports coercion under torture. The family refuses, so the record must not imply that any of them complied.
additions.audience: the seven brothers and their mother

additional_scripture.context_note: The torturers renew the demand to the second brother and he refuses.

additions.title: The fourth brother counsels looking to God for resurrection when facing death
additions.reason: A ‘preferable’ saying on facing death with hope in God; the judgment on the king is context. Compare AUD-16-9-11’s ‘it is right’ saying.
additions.speaker_or_source: the fourth brother, as he was dying

additions.title: Judas divides the army and appoints Simon, Joseph, and Jonathan as leaders
additions.reason: Verses 21–23 report the division into four sections, name the three brothers, and say Judas himself led the first company. Eleazar is also mentioned, without a separate command stated for him in this wording.
additions.audience: Simon, Joseph, and Jonathan and the companies entrusted to them

additions.title: Antiochus orders his charioteer to drive on without stopping toward Jerusalem
additions.reason: Reported royal order, renewed in 9:7 (‘ordering the journey hastened’); his boast is context. Reference adds 9:7.

additions.title: Antiochus Eupator appoints Lysias chief minister and governor of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia
additions.reason: Narrated royal appointment, like published AUD-15-10-65; distinct from Antiochus IV’s regency charge to Lysias (AUD-15-3-32).
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Maccabeus leaves Simon, Joseph and Zacchaeus to besiege the two towers
additions.reason: Narrated assignment of a besieging force, like published AUD-15-4-41; the bribery and executions that follow are narrative.
additions.audience: Simon, Joseph and Zacchaeus with their men

additions.title: Judas urges his men to share the danger and help their brothers
additions.reason: Reported battle exhortation on a new occasion (Beth-zur), as the catalogue records Judas’s others (AUD-16-8-16, AUD-16-13-14).

additions.title: Lysias urges the Jews to settle on every just condition
additions.reason: Lysias's message urging settlement (11:14) is the direction; 11:13 and 11:15 narrate, and 11:16–21 is a letter of report and conditional promise (independent check).
additions.speaker_or_source: Lysias, the king’s guardian and chief minister

additions.title: Roman envoys ask the Jews to send representatives quickly with their position
additions.reason: Explicit requests by letter (‘send someone immediately… hurry and send some men’); no record covers the Roman letter.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
additions.speaker_or_source: Quintus Memmius and Titus Manius, Roman envoys, by letter

additions.title: The defeated Arab nomads ask Judas for pledges
additions.reason: Reported request for peace pledges, granted in 12:12; such petitions are recorded nearby (ot-1-maccabees-v11-50).

additions.title: Judas’s party urges Scythopolis to continue its goodwill toward the Jews
additions.reason: The narrative reports thanks and a request for future goodwill. The speech is an appeal, with no quoted order.

additions.title: The narrator commends atonement for the fallen in hope of resurrection
additions.reason: The narrator explicitly explains why Judas’s action made sense in light of resurrection and commends his intent. The passage teaches through the action rather than quoting a general command.

additions.title: Antiochus Eupator orders Menelaus taken to Beroea and put to death
additions.reason: Explicit reported execution order; 13:5–8 describe the local custom and its justice and stay as context.
additions.speaker_or_source: King Antiochus Eupator, at Lysias’s prompting

additions.title: Judas stations armed men to guard the conference against treachery
additions.reason: The narrative names a specific guard assignment and its stated purpose. No formal spoken instruction is quoted.

additions.title: Nicanor urges Judas to marry and have children
additions.reason: Nicanor urges Judas personally to marry and have children. The text reports advice and Judas’s response rather than a general rule.

additions.title: Nicanor orders the priests to hand over Judas, threatening the temple
additions.reason: Verses 31–33 report Nicanor’s demand and sworn threat against the temple. The same encounter is told with different wording in 1 Maccabees.

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel also threatens to burn the temple unless Judas is handed over, and includes Judas’s army in the demand.

additions.title: Nicanor sends more than five hundred soldiers to arrest Razis
additions.reason: Reported sending of troops to arrest Razis, a hostile order like AUD-16-5-11; 14:40 states its purpose.
additions.audience: The more than five hundred soldiers Nicanor sent

additions.title: Nicanor commands arms taken up on the Sabbath for the king’s business
additions.reason: Nicanor’s explicit counter-command answering 15:2–4; a hostile order distinct from the Jews’ recorded plea (ot-2-maccabees-v15-2).
additions.audience: his army, including the Jews compelled to accompany him

additions.title: Judas orders Nicanor’s head and hand brought to Jerusalem and his tongue given to birds
additions.reason: Verse 30 reports the order to sever and carry the head and hand. Verse 33 distinguishes Judas cutting out the tongue himself from his order to give it to the birds and hang the trophies.
additions.audience: Judas’s men charged with carrying out the orders

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel reports the head and right hand being cut off and displayed outside Jerusalem, without quoting all the orders in 2 Maccabees.

additions.title: The returned leaders appoint Levites aged twenty and up to supervise the temple work
additions.reason: Narrated appointment of Levites over the rebuilding, like published AUD-14-31-2; Ezra 3 has no record.
additions.audience: the Levites from twenty years old and upward
additions.speaker_or_source: Zorobabel, Iesous and the returned priests and Levites

additions.title: Officials ask Artaxerxes to search his predecessors’ records about Jerusalem
additions.reason: Verse 15 contains the stated request for a records search. Stopping the work is the king’s later ruling, and not an explicit request of the letter.
additions.speaker_or_source: Raoum the baaltam, Samsai the scribe and their colleagues, by letter

additions.title: Thanthanai and his colleagues ask Darius to search for Cyrus’s decree and report back
additions.reason: Explicit petition to the king to search the archives and reply; no record covers the letter’s request.
additions.speaker_or_source: Thanthanai the governor, Satharbouzana and their colleagues, by letter

additions.title: Darius decrees a search of the royal archives in Babylon
additions.reason: Royal decree granting the 5:17 request, like AUD-19-6-1 (records searched by royal order); the scroll found is context.

additions.title: The returned exiles station priests and Levites in divisions for temple service
additions.reason: The returned community makes the appointments in accordance with Moses’s book. The passage attributes these specific staffing actions to the community and does not quote a new divine appointment.
additions.speaker_or_source: The returned community implementing the book of Moses

additions.title: Ezra and family heads are set apart to examine the foreign marriages
additions.reason: Verse 16 reports the named appointments to examine the marriages as implementation of the earlier assembly proposal. It does not add a new law.
additions.audience: Ezra the priest and the heads of ancestral houses

additions.title: Abimelech’s party asks Isaac to swear a covenant of nonaggression
additions.reason: The visitors propose an oath and specify doing no harm. Verse 31 reports that the parties subsequently swear to one another.

additions.title: The Egyptians ask Joseph to buy them and their land and give them seed
additions.speaker_or_source: Egyptians seeking food during the famine
additions.reason: This famine petition follows and differs from their earlier plea and the exchange of livestock for food. They now propose giving themselves and their land for bread and request seed.

additions.title: Jacob warns Reuben against his insolence
additions.audience: Reuben, as Jacob addresses his sons
additions.reason: In the Saints text Jacob warns Reuben not to boil over. This poetic rebuke is tied to the violation of his father’s bed.

additions.title: The Lord appoints Moses to relay His words and Aaron to speak to Pharaoh
additions.audience: Moses, with Aaron assigned to speak to Pharaoh
additions.reason: The Lord specifies each brother’s role in the mission to seek Israel’s release. Pharaoh’s separately addressed obligation to release Israel already has a record.

additional_scripture.context_note: The Lord explicitly charges Moses and Aaron concerning Pharaoh and Israel’s departure.

additions.title: The Lord sends Moses down and directs him to return with Aaron
additions.audience: Moses, with Aaron to accompany him on the return
additions.reason: The Lord sends Moses down from Sinai and limits who may return with him. The priests and people are not to force their way up.

additions.title: Aaron proclaims a feast before the golden calf
additions.reason: Aaron announces the feast in the Lord’s name after erecting the calf’s altar. The surrounding narrative attributes the proclamation to Aaron and describes the worship as lawless.

additions.title: Moses summons Bezalel, Eliab, and the willing skilled workers for sanctuary work
additions.audience: Bezalel, Eliab, and the willing skilled workers
additions.speaker_or_source: Moses, implementing the Lord’s sanctuary instructions
additions.reason: Moses calls the workers to undertake the sanctuary work and gives them the contributions. The distinct appointment and divine gift of skill are reported earlier.

additions.title: Moses tells Aaron’s remaining sons to eat the sin offering in the holy place
additions.audience: Eleazar and Ithamar, with Aaron replying for the household
additions.speaker_or_source: Moses, citing the Lord’s earlier direction
additions.reason: Moses applies the prior rule to the congregation’s goat, whose blood had not gone into the holy place. Aaron explains the exceptional circumstances, and Moses accepts his explanation.

additions.title: The Israelites propose appointing a leader and going back to Egypt
additions.audience: One another in the complaining congregation
additions.reason: The people urge a return and propose appointing a leader. This is their rebellious proposal, not an appointment that was carried out.

additions.title: God keeps His word and carries out what He has spoken
additions.audience: Balak and the assembled officials of Moab
additions.speaker_or_source: Balaam, in the oracle the Lord gave him
additions.reason: The oracle contrasts God with human unreliability. Verses 16–18 identify the source and setting, while the next verse applies that faithfulness to the blessing Balaam cannot reverse.

additions.title: Moses appoints leaders and recording officers from the tribes
additions.audience: The qualified men appointed to lead the tribes and serve their judges
additions.reason: Moses recalls carrying out the specific appointments after the people agreed to choose qualified men. The subsequent directions to the judges have their own records.

additions.title: Israel will find the Lord when it seeks Him wholeheartedly in distress
additions.audience: Israel, including those who would later be scattered
additions.speaker_or_source: Moses, teaching Israel about the Lord’s mercy and covenant
additions.reason: Moses speaks of repentance and seeking the Lord in a future time of dispersion, grounding hope in the Lord’s mercy and covenant faithfulness.

additions.title: Recognize the Lord as faithful to His covenant and just in His judgment
additions.speaker_or_source: Moses, teaching Israel about the Lord
additions.reason: Moses teaches Israel to recognize the Lord’s faithfulness, covenant mercy, and response to those who hate Him. The immediate setting is His prior deliverance of Israel.

additions.title: Be perfect before the Lord in allegiance to Him
additions.audience: Israel about to enter the land
additions.speaker_or_source: Moses, delivering the Lord’s instructions to Israel
additions.reason: The Saints wording calls Israel to be perfect before the Lord. The surrounding verses contrast this allegiance with the nations’ dependence on divination and direct Israel toward the prophet God raises up.

additions.title: Joshua teaches Israel to trust that the Lord’s promises and warnings will come to pass
additions.audience: Israel and its leaders in Joshua’s farewell
additions.reason: Joshua recalls the fulfillment of the Lord’s good words and uses it to warn that the covenant penalties will likewise follow disobedience.

additions.title: Boaz tells Ruth not to fear and explains that a nearer kinsman exists
additions.reason: Boaz’s personal reassurance answers Ruth’s request. He promises help and identifies the nearer kinsman before giving the separate instruction to lodge overnight.

additions.title: Samuel tells Saul to stop worrying about his lost donkeys
additions.reason: Samuel explicitly tells Saul not to set his heart on the animals because they have been found. This is separate from the invitation to the meal.

additions.title: Samuel warns that Israel and its king must follow the Lord together
additions.audience: Israel and its newly appointed king
additions.reason: Samuel names both the people and their king and warns that the Lord will oppose them if they disregard His voice. The warning is distinct from the sign Samuel next asks them to witness.

additions.title: David appoints singers for the Lord’s house after the ark comes to rest
additions.audience: The singers David appointed for sanctuary service
additions.reason: The account attributes the appointments to David, describes the singers’ prescribed service, and begins naming them.

additions.title: David makes the men who joined him leaders of his forces
additions.audience: The men of Benjamin and Judah who came to David’s aid
additions.reason: David receives the men after Amasai’s declaration and explicitly appoints them as leaders of the forces.

additions.title: Sennacherib’s message quotes Hezekiah directing worship at one altar
additions.audience: Judah and Jerusalem, as the Assyrian message describes them
additions.speaker_or_source: Hezekiah, as quoted in Sennacherib’s message
additions.reason: The hostile speech attributes this local worship instruction to Hezekiah. This record preserves the attribution and its rhetorical setting.

additional_scripture.context_note: The Assyrian envoy similarly quotes Hezekiah directing Judah and Jerusalem to bow down before one altar.
This parallel also presents the altar instruction as an accusation in the Assyrian envoy’s speech.

additions.title: Levite overseers are appointed to supervise temple repairs under Josiah
additions.audience: Jeth, Abdias, Zacharias, Mosollam, and the Levites overseeing workers
additions.speaker_or_source: The Chronicler reports the appointments without naming the appointing official
additions.reason: The text names the overseers and their assignment. It describes the appointments without identifying who appointed each person.

additions.title: Judas appoints commanders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens
additions.audience: The leaders Judas appoints over the people
additions.reason: Verse 55 explicitly assigns the command roles. The military exemptions applied in the following verse have a separate record.

additions.title: Ptolemy asks Demetrius to make a covenant and offers his daughter in marriage
additions.reason: Ptolemy sends a concrete covenant proposal and names what he offers Demetrius. The narrator explains the rivalry behind the proposal.

additions.title: It is right to remember brothers in worship and prayer
additions.audience: The Spartans addressed in Jonathan’s letter
additions.speaker_or_source: Jonathan, speaking for the senders of the letter
additions.reason: The letter explicitly calls remembrance of brothers right and fitting and describes the prayers, sacrifices, and appointed days in which the senders remember them.

additions.title: Tryphon orders his officials and forces to obey Jonathan
additions.reason: Tryphon explicitly tells his subordinates to obey Jonathan as they obey him. His later order to Jonathan to dismiss the troops has a different recipient.

additions.title: Nehemiah orders the remaining water poured over larger stones
additions.speaker_or_source: Nehemiah, in the account reported by the letter
additions.reason: The narrative reports a specific order after the sacrificial materials are consumed. It distinguishes the remaining water from the earlier use of the liquid on the offerings.

additions.title: Heliodorus warns the king what will happen to anyone sent to harm the temple
additions.audience: The king who asks whom to send to Jerusalem
additions.reason: Heliodorus replies with pointed counsel about whom to send and warns of divine judgment against those who try to harm the temple.

additions.title: The youngest brother warns Antiochus against pride and points to God’s judgment
additions.speaker_or_source: The youngest of the seven brothers
additions.reason: His direct admonition against arrogance is followed by an account of why the king has not escaped divine judgment. It differs from the brother’s earlier refusal to obey the royal ordinance.

additions.title: Lysias commissions delegates to explain the terms to the Jews
additions.audience: The men named earlier in the letter and Lysias’s own representatives
additions.reason: Lysias explicitly reports that he has instructed both groups to speak to the Jews concerning the matters and particulars. The earlier proposal to settle remains a separate appeal.

additions.title: Jehoshaphat appoints singers to give thanks before the army
additions.audience: The psalm singers and others appointed to give praise
additions.speaker_or_source: King Jehoshaphat, after consulting the people
additions.reason: The king explicitly appoints the singers and describes their role. Their praise accompanies the army and follows his separate exhortation in verse 20.

additions.title: The king appoints Nehemiah governor of Judah
additions.speaker_or_source: King Arthasastha, identified in Nehemiah’s report
additions.reason: Nehemiah reports receiving authority as governor and identifies the king’s reign. His earlier request at 2:5–6 concerned the mission to rebuild Jerusalem, whereas this verse names the governing office.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Gatekeepers, singers and Levites are appointed after the wall is built
additions.audience: The appointed gatekeepers, singers and Levites
additions.speaker_or_source: Nehemiah reports the appointments without naming the person who made them
additions.reason: The verse expressly reports the appointments. Nehemiah separately says he put up the doors, and the passive appointment clause does not name an appointing speaker.

additions.title: Nehemiah stations two praise companies at the wall’s dedication
additions.audience: The two praise companies, accompanied by Judah’s leaders and people
additions.reason: Verse 31 states Nehemiah positioned the two groups. Verses 38–40 identify the second group and show both performing at the dedication.

additions.title: Nehemiah assigns service divisions for the priests and Levites
additions.audience: The priests and Levites restored to their respective service divisions
additions.reason: Nehemiah reports establishing service divisions, each according to its work. Verse 31 separately recalls provisions and includes a prayer.

additions.title: Artaxerxes orders the stewards to carry out his and the guests’ wishes
additions.reason: The narrator reports the king’s order for this feast and distinguishes it from established law.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Artaxerxes orders Mordecai’s loyalty recorded in the royal library

additions.reason: Esther summons and sends her attendant with the specific task of learning the matter from Mordecai. The messenger’s assignment precedes Esther’s later reply.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Esther invites Artaxerxes and Haman to her reception that day
additions.audience: Artaxerxes, with Haman invited through him
additions.reason: Esther addresses her conditional request to the king and names Haman as the other guest.

additions.reason: The king issues a separate instruction to hurry Haman to the reception in response to Esther’s invitation.

additions.reason: The request is addressed directly to the king and names Haman as the other guest. It concerns the next day, distinct from the first reception in verse 4.
additions.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

additions.title: Artaxerxes authorizes Esther’s request and orders Haman’s sons hanged
additions.audience: The Jews of Susa charged with carrying out the order
additions.reason: The narrator reports the king’s permission and published order to hang the bodies. Esther’s preceding request in verse 13 remains a separate utterance.

additions.title: Job urges the faithful to hold their way and take courage
additions.audience: Job’s companions in the dialogue, concerning the faithful and clean-handed
additions.reason: The optative exhortations occur within Job’s lament and commend upright perseverance.

additions.title: Job’s oath treats neglect of the needy as wrongdoing
additions.audience: Job’s hearers, with God invoked in his defense
additions.reason: Job names care of the poor, widow, orphan and naked in his oath and gives fear of the Lord as his motive. The passage sets out the ethics of his defense rather than issuing a general statute.

additions.title: Job disavows trusting riches and deceptive homage
additions.audience: Job’s hearers, with God invoked in his defense
additions.reason: Job’s conditional oath expressly rejects misplaced trust and the concealed action he calls lawlessness before God. The Saints wording does not explicitly name the sun and moon as objects of worship.

additions.title: A needy person longs for gladness, wine and oil
additions.reason: The wording describes a needy person’s desires and should not be paraphrased as a causal claim that pleasure always produces poverty.

additions.title: The bloodthirsty hate the holy, but the upright seek his life
additions.speaker_or_source: The wisdom teacher in the collection copied by Hezekiah’s circle
additions.reason: Preserves the contrast in the Saints wording without resolving the idiom ‘seek his life’ beyond what the verse states.

additions.title: The Lord orders Canaan’s strength destroyed in the Tyre oracle

additions.title: The judgment oracle calls for wailing over vanished wine

additions.speaker_or_source: Isaiah delivering the Lord’s judgment oracle

additions.title: The Lord calls for His message to be proclaimed in Judah

additions.title: Israel’s enemies urge one another not to release the captives

additions.audience: The angel of the Lord, with Daniel receiving understanding

additions.reason: The Saints account explicitly says the angel gave a spirit of understanding to Daniel as commanded. The commission is reported through its execution.

additions.title: The king hands Daniel over under pressure from the crowd
additions.audience: The king’s companions, before the hostile crowd

additions.reason: The Saints text explicitly names the messenger and tells him to go and speak. Esther receives the warning inside the message, while Achrathaeus receives the assignment to deliver it.

additions.title: Habakkuk models rejoicing in God amid crop and livestock failure
additions.audience: Hearers of Habakkuk’s prayer song in a time of affliction
additions.reason: The poetic contrast deliberately presents the prophet’s trust and rejoicing when every ordinary source of food fails. The speaker models a response without issuing a direct command.

additions.audience: Zechariah, sent to speak to the people
additions.reason: The Lord explicitly instructs Zechariah to say the message to the people. The current command row addresses the people’s separate obligation to return.

additions.audience: The Syrophoenician woman appealing for her daughter
additions.speaker_or_source: Jesus, in dialogue with the Syrophoenician woman
additions.reason: The two speakers deliberately reason through a table image about the priority of the children and the woman’s appeal. Jesus commends her answer by granting the request. The healing dismissal belongs to the episode.

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel names her a Canaanite woman and explicitly commends her faith. Matthew also records Jesus’ statement about His mission to the lost sheep of Israel.

additions.title: The interrogators demand that the healed man give glory to God
additions.audience: The man who had been blind
additions.speaker_or_source: The interrogators who call him back
additions.reason: The interrogators tell the healed man to give glory to God, asserting that Jesus is a sinner. He answers with the fact of his healing. The exchange follows their separate threat of exclusion in 9:22.

additions.title: Affliction can produce perseverance, proven character and hope
additions.reason: Paul presents a progression from affliction through perseverance and tested character to hope, grounded in God’s love poured out through the Spirit. The teaching is distinct from his Adam and Christ comparison later in the chapter.

additions.title: Paul describes walking by faith and aiming to please the Lord
additions.audience: The Corinthians and the saints in Achaia to whom the letter is sent
additions.speaker_or_source: Paul, describing the aim of himself and his fellow workers
additions.reason: Paul presents faith rather than sight and the aim of pleasing the Lord as the practical posture of the passage. He connects it to appearing before Christ’s judgment seat. The later commission to reconcile is distinct.

additions.title: Distinguish sincere zeal from attempts to isolate you
additions.reason: Paul contrasts zeal that seeks to isolate the Galatians from him with zeal for a good purpose even when he is absent. The teaching concerns manipulative attention and is distinct from the catalogue’s broader circumcision warning.

additions.title: Greet every saint in Christ Jesus at Philippi
additions.audience: The believers receiving the letter in Philippi
additions.reason: The first clause requests a greeting; the next clause reports greetings from Paul’s companions. No holy kiss is specified.

additions.title: Archippus: see that you fulfill the ministry you received in the Lord
additions.audience: Archippus, with the Colossians asked to relay the charge
additions.reason: The task belongs to Archippus; the congregation is instructed to relay it. The passage does not specify the ministry’s duties.

additions.title: Greet Prisca, Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus
additions.audience: Timothy, relaying greetings to the named people
additions.reason: The imperative directs Timothy to greet these people and is distinct from the later greetings sent to Timothy.

additions.title: Greet those who love us in faith
additions.audience: Titus as the recipient charged to pass on the greeting
additions.reason: The end of the letter distinguishes greetings sent by Paul’s company from the greeting Titus is asked to convey.

additions.title: Be diligent to enter God’s rest and avoid the pattern of disobedience
additions.audience: Readers of Hebrews, addressed as holy brothers and sisters
additions.reason: The writer urges the hearers in verses 1 and 11 and develops a specific application of the wilderness example to the remaining promise of rest.

additional_scripture.context_note: The living word of God judges the heart, and every person is accountable before Him.
The psalm supplies the Today warning and the oath about entering God’s rest; Hebrews applies it to the hearers.

additions.title: Learn from the faith of Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, and Jacob
additions.audience: Readers of Hebrews, addressed as holy brothers and sisters
additions.reason: The author illustrates faith through obedience, waiting, trusting God’s promise, and blessing what is still to come. These are examples, not new commands to repeat their actions.

additions.title: Joseph looked ahead to the exodus, and Moses’ parents acted in faith despite the decree
additions.audience: Readers of Hebrews, addressed as holy brothers and sisters
additions.reason: The author supplies two examples of faith distinct from Moses’ own choices in verses 24–27. Joseph’s instructions concerning his bones and the king’s decree remain distinct historical directions.

additional_scripture.context_note: Joseph makes the sons of Israel swear to carry his bones away when God visits them.
The account narrates how Moses was hidden, then placed in a basket.

additions.title: Learn from Rahab and the faithful who endured without seeing fulfillment
additions.audience: Readers of Hebrews, addressed as holy brothers and sisters
additions.reason: The writer gives Rahab’s welcome, the judges and prophets, and the endurance of sufferers as examples of faith. Israel at the sea and Jericho in verses 29–30 are connected examples, but no new directive.

additions.title: False teachers exploit their hearers with destructive teaching
additions.audience: Readers who received faith with the apostles (2 Peter 1:1)
additions.speaker_or_source: The writer who identifies himself as Simeon Peter
additions.reason: This warning identifies denial of the Master, exploitation, and the teachers’ judgment. It is an instructive warning, with no separately quoted imperative.

additional_scripture.context_note: Jude similarly warns of intruders who deny the Master; Jude’s distinct charge is to contend for the faith.

additions.title: Recognize greed and arrogance in the example of Balaam and the false teachers
additions.audience: Readers who received faith with the apostles (2 Peter 1:1)
additions.speaker_or_source: The writer who identifies himself as Simeon Peter
additions.reason: The author contrasts abusive conduct with angelic restraint and names Balaam as a warning against gain from wrongdoing.

additional_scripture.context_note: Jude similarly contrasts abusive speech with angelic restraint and uses Balaam as a negative example.

additions.title: Gaius: greet the friends by name
additions.reason: The elder reports greetings from the friends and gives Gaius a distinct charge to greet his friends by name.

additions.title: Learn from Michael’s restraint in contrast with slanderous speech
additions.audience: Those called, beloved in God, and kept for Jesus Christ (Jude 1:1)
additions.reason: Michael appeals to the Lord rather than bringing a slanderous judgment. The story contrasts him with the people Jude rebukes.

additional_scripture.context_note: The parallel contrasts arrogant slander with the restraint of angels without naming Michael.

additions.title: The four living creatures call “Come” as the first four seals open
additions.audience: The text does not name the immediate addressee of the four calls
additions.speaker_or_source: The four living creatures in John’s vision
additions.reason: Each opening has the same utterance from a different living creature; the separate voice of verse 6 limits harm to oil and wine.

additions.title: Rejoice and give God glory at the marriage of the Lamb
additions.audience: Fellow worshippers in the vision; no narrower recipient is named
additions.speaker_or_source: The voice John hears as of a great multitude
additions.reason: The multitude gives a distinct call to rejoice at the wedding. The voice from the throne in verse 5 addresses God’s servants.

set.title: Moses entrusts Israel’s leaders with carrying out the eastern tribes’ campaign agreement

set.original_audience_or_recipient: His attendants
